This facility at 1401 Russell Street in Baltimore, Maryland, recorded here under the name of the business park it sits within, Baltimore Technology Park, is operated as a data center by TierPoint, a national colocation and managed IT services provider. The address sits in Baltimore's Camden Yards area, part of an enterprise zone that has drawn conversions of older industrial and warehouse buildings into modern commercial and technical space, a pattern common in East Coast cities where existing structures near downtown offer power access, loading capacity, and connectivity that would be expensive to replicate from scratch.

According to TierPoint's own published specifications, the Baltimore facility offers more than 28,000 total square feet, including over 14,000 square feet of raised floor colocation space, organized as a dual, A side and B side power distribution design intended to keep customer equipment running even if one electrical path fails. Backup power comes from two 1.5 megawatt generators that TierPoint states can run for a minimum of 48 hours without refueling, paired with a 100 percent uptime service level agreement. The site is carrier neutral, meaning customers can choose among multiple independent network and fiber providers rather than being locked into a single carrier, and TierPoint describes DWDM connectivity linking this location to another TierPoint facility for additional network diversity.

Physical security includes round the clock staffing, electronic surveillance, two factor biometric authentication for facility access, and closed circuit camera footage retained for a minimum of ninety days. On the compliance side, TierPoint states the facility is audited annually against SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II standards, along with SOC 2 plus HITRUST, GLBA, HIPAA, and PCI DSS frameworks relevant to healthcare, financial, and payment card customers, and holds ISO 27001 certification along with ITAR and Data Privacy Framework registration, credentials aimed at customers in defense, government, and international data transfer contexts. Services offered from the site include colocation, managed IT, private cloud, disaster recovery, security solutions, and 24 by 7 remote hands support. Taken together, the specifications published by TierPoint describe a genuine, actively operated regional data center, not merely an address inside a business park that happens to carry a technology sounding name.

reading.body:
Baltimore Technology Park operates a 28,000-square-foot regional colocation facility in downtown Baltimore with over 14,000 square feet of raised floor space on a dual A/B power architecture. The site draws backup power from two 1.5-megawatt generators, each capable of 48-hour runtime without refuel. The operator publishes no IT power load figure, so the capacity available for customer equipment cannot be estimated from the data given.

The facility holds SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II certifications, qualifying it for regulated financial and healthcare workloads. It also holds ISO 27001, ITAR registration, and Data Privacy Framework certification, qualifying it for defense, government, and international transfer customers. These credentials indicate the site is built to serve compliance-sensitive customers rather than hyperscaler density play.

In Maryland, 11 facilities are mapped in open data and 3 report published power capacity totaling 9.3 megawatts. Baltimore Technology Park ranks fourth by published megawatts in the state. The absence of a power figure from this operator means Maryland's true capacity is unknown and this facility's actual position in state hierarchy cannot be assessed. For AI scaling decisions, this site is a small regional colocation venue, not a hyperscaler campus or a grid-scale power consumer.
